practices.name: Theme verse reflection (upasamanussati)
practices.howto: Sit. Recite the theme verse slowly, in Pali then English: stilling of preparations, relinquishment of assets, destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction. Rest attention on each phrase for three breaths. Do not analyse. Let each phrase land. When the mind argues, return to the next phrase. Ten minutes.
practices.source_note: Sermon 1 theme verse (Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ). Upasamanussati — reflection on peace as meditation subject. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.
These are introductions drawn from the sermons; deeper practice is learned with a qualified teacher. Satsang lists places to practise.

practices.name: Locating the wound (craving in the body)
practices.howto: Sit. When craving arises for anything, do not follow it to its object. Instead ask: where in the body is this felt? Chest? Throat? Belly? Rest attention on the location, not the story. The location is the wound. The story is the arrow's feathers. Ten minutes, or until the craving shifts.
practices.source_note: Sermon 1 wound-and-surgeon simile (acchecchi tanham idha namarupe). The bandage goes on the wound. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.
If you have a history of trauma, dissociation, psychosis or severe anxiety, keep sits short with eyes open, or practise with a qualified teacher or clinician.

practices.name: Fire going out (extinction contemplation)
practices.howto: Light a candle, or picture one. Watch the flame. It burns because of fuel and air meeting. Now imagine the fuel running out — not blown out, just exhausted. The flame doesn't go anywhere. It stops happening. Sit with that image for ten minutes. Then close the eyes and feel the body's own little fires: hunger, wanting, restlessness. Same mechanism.
practices.source_note: Sermon 1 fire simile (Aggivacchagotta). Wood burns because of fire, fire because of wood — this-to-that relatedness. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: Never leave a lit candle unattended; picturing the flame works as well.
If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.

practices.name: Seeing the root pattern (mula-pariyaya)
practices.howto: Pick one sense door — hearing is easiest. For five minutes, notice each sound and the instant 'I' gets added: 'I hear it,' 'I like it,' 'I want it to stop.' Just notice the adding. Don't stop it. The noticing IS the practice. The 'I' is a postscript, not the text.
practices.source_note: Sermon 13 mula-pariyaya. Conceiving earth as earth, delighting, 'I am earth' — the full proliferation in one sutta. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.

practices.name: Only the seen (Bahiya instruction)
practices.howto: Choose one sense — sight is clearest. For ten minutes: in the seen, only the seen. When 'I see it' arises, drop the 'I', keep the seeing. When commentary starts, drop it, keep the colours and shapes. This is not suppression — it is subtraction. The seeing was always just seeing.
practices.source_note: Sermon 15 Bahiya instruction. No experiencer added to experience. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.

practices.name: Looking for the observer
practices.howto: Sit in signless rest. Then ask, gently: who is resting? Who is aware? Look for the looker. Do not answer with philosophy — look. If you find tension, a watcher-feeling, a subtle 'me' holding the sit together — notice it as one more sign. Let it be there without serving it. Ten minutes. The looking is the practice; there is no finding.
practices.source_note: Sermons 16-17. The observer is the last sign. Seeing through it is the last gate. From Ven. Kaṭukurunde Ñāṇananda, Nibbāna: The Mind Stilled (free at seeingthroughthenet.net). Satsang summary in its own words.
